display.title: Display
display.about: How the game window opens and how its picture is drawn.
display.performance_mode_on: Performance mode is on, so antialiasing stays off.
display.this_run_windowed: This run: {{width}} x {{height}}, {{aspect}}, windowed, {{frame_rate}} (command line, not saved)
display.this_run_fullscreen: This run: {{width}} x {{height}}, {{aspect}}, fullscreen, {{frame_rate}} (command line, not saved)

mode.name: Mode
mode.about: Fullscreen covers the whole display, at the resolution below.

resolution.name: Resolution
resolution.window_about: The window's size, from those your graphics card offers for this display.
resolution.window_about_remembered: The window's size, from those your graphics card offers for this display. The game also keeps the size and place you leave its window at.
resolution.screen_about: The screen's resolution. Desktop keeps the display's own; another switches the display to it while the game runs.

aspect_ratio.name: Aspect ratio
aspect_ratio.about: 16:9 is the game's widescreen layout and 4:3 its original one; both keep their shape. Stretch fills the whole screen.

wider_view.name: Wider view
wider_view.about: In matches on a screen wider or taller than 16:9, shows more of the stadium instead of bars, with the HUD in the 16:9 middle. Menus keep their 16:9 picture.

resolution.name: 3D resolution
resolution.about: Full draws the game at the resolution above, the sharpest. Native is the Wii's 640 x 448; 2x-4x are its multiples, for slower graphics cards.

antialiasing.name: Antialiasing
antialiasing.about: Smooths jagged edges. The stronger kinds cost more GPU time.

style.name: Picture style
style.about: Modern draws the game's picture crisp, straight into the window. Original TV adds the Wii's flicker filter and a TV's softness.

tv_border.name: TV border
tv_border.about: The empty border a Wii sends around its picture, which a TV hides.

upscaling.name: Upscaling
upscaling.about: How a 3D resolution other than Full reaches the resolution above. Sharp keeps pixels square.

vsync.name: VSync
vsync.about: Synchronizes frames with your display to prevent tearing.

frame_rate.name: Frame rate
frame_rate.about: Original is the console's 60 FPS. Higher rates draw more frames for smoother motion while the game keeps its own speed; Display follows your display's refresh rate.

throttle.name: Throttle in background
throttle.about: Draws fewer frames while the game's window is minimized or another window has the focus, to save power. The full frame rate returns as soon as you go back.

background_frame_rate.name: Background frame rate
background_frame_rate.about: The frames per second at most while the game is in the background.

overlay.title: Performance overlay
overlay.about: FPS and system GPU and CPU usage; in network games the latency, and with rollback the input delay (DLY) and rollback frames (RB).

on_screen.name: On screen
on_screen.about: A compact row in a corner, also in fullscreen. Latency shows N/A until online play is available.

aspect_note.saved_auto: Saved value auto: 16:9 or 4:3, whichever is closer to the screen's shape ({{shape}} here). Choose one above to change it.
aspect_note.saved_unsupported: Saved value {{value}} is not supported by the game. Choose one above.
aspect_note.stretch_window: Uses the {{shape}} layout and fills the window at any size, stretching the picture with it.
aspect_note.stretch_display: Uses the {{shape}} layout and fills the whole display.
aspect_note.stretch_exactly: Uses the {{shape}} layout, which fills this {{size}} display exactly.
aspect_note.stretch_wider: Uses the {{shape}} layout and fills this {{size}} display; the picture is {{percent}}% wider than {{shape}}.
aspect_note.stretch_narrower: Uses the {{shape}} layout and fills this {{size}} display; the picture is {{percent}}% narrower than {{shape}}.
aspect_note.wider_window: The window can take any shape: in matches the wider view fills it with more of the stadium.
aspect_note.wider_sides: In matches, fills this {{size}} display with more of the stadium at the sides. Menus keep 16:9.
aspect_note.wider_above: In matches, fills this {{size}} display with more of the stadium above and below. Menus keep 16:9.
aspect_note.window_keeps: The window keeps the {{shape}} shape when you resize it, so the picture fills it. Maximized on a screen of another shape, it shows bars.
aspect_note.bars_sides_one: On this {{size}} display: bars of {{count}} pixel left and right.
aspect_note.bars_sides_other: On this {{size}} display: bars of {{count}} pixels left and right.
aspect_note.bars_above_one: On this {{size}} display: bars of {{count}} pixel above and below.
aspect_note.bars_above_other: On this {{size}} display: bars of {{count}} pixels above and below.
aspect_note.stretch_or_wider_fills: Stretch or the wider view fills it.

resolution_note.fewer_screen: {{name}}: {{width}} x {{height}}, fewer pixels than the picture on this screen.
resolution_note.fewer_window: {{name}}: {{width}} x {{height}}, fewer pixels than the picture on this window.
resolution_note.more_screen: {{name}}: {{width}} x {{height}}, more pixels than the picture on this screen.
resolution_note.more_window: {{name}}: {{width}} x {{height}}, more pixels than the picture on this window.
resolution_note.as_many_screen: {{name}}: {{width}} x {{height}}, about as many pixels as the picture on this screen.
resolution_note.as_many_window: {{name}}: {{width}} x {{height}}, about as many pixels as the picture on this window.

frame_rate_note.vsync_holds: VSync holds it to this display's {{hz}} Hz.
frame_rate_note.cannot_show_all: This display refreshes at {{hz}} Hz, so it cannot show every frame.
frame_rate_note.no_limit: No limit: the game draws as fast as your computer allows.

off.name: Off
off.about: No smoothing. The lightest on the graphics card.

fxaa.name: FXAA
fxaa.about: Smooths edges in the finished picture. Nearly free, but softens fine detail and text a little.

msaa.name: 4x MSAA
msaa.about: Smooths the edges of 3D shapes (4x multisampling). Costs some GPU time.

msaa_fxaa.name: 4x MSAA + FXAA
msaa_fxaa.about: 4x MSAA, then FXAA for the edges it leaves, such as those inside textures.

ssaa.name: 4x SSAA
ssaa.about: Shades all 4 samples of each pixel: also smooths edges inside textures, such as stripes on banners. Costs the most GPU time.

window_size.too_large: More than a window can take on this display: the game opens it at {{width}} x {{height}}, the largest that fits.
window_size.not_shape: Not {{shape}}: the game opens it at {{width}} x {{height}}, the picture's shape.

fullscreen_resolution.no_such_mode: This display has no such mode, so fullscreen keeps the display's own resolution.
fullscreen_resolution.other_shape: Another shape than this {{size}} display: some displays stretch it; others show bars.

audio.title: Audio
audio.about: The game's volume and the level of each kind of sound. The music, sound effect and voice settings in the game's own Options menu still apply.

output.title: Output
output.about: Plays through your system's default audio device.

master_volume.name: Master volume
master_volume.about: Scales the game's speaker output, like the volume of a TV.

mute.name: Mute
mute.about: Silences the game without changing the volume.

sound_levels.title: Sound levels
sound_levels.about: Each kind of sound as a share of the level the game gives it, on the PC only. Applies when the game starts.

reset.name: Reset levels
reset.about: Every kind of sound back to 100%, the game's own mix.

controls.title: Controls
controls.about: Play with keyboard and mouse, an Xbox, PlayStation or other gamepad, or a Wii Remote with Nunchuk. Keep the game window focused.

players.title: Players
players.about: Players fill in order and each controller plays once. Changes apply when the game starts.
players.dolphinbar_mode_tooltip: The DolphinBar is in a mouse or gamepad mode. Press its MODE button until light 4 is on.
players.no_access_tooltip: A Wii Remote is connected, but this user can't open it.
players.no_remote_hint: Pair one over Bluetooth, or use a Mayflash DolphinBar in mode 4.
players.missing_tooltip: Not connected. Connect it before you start the game.
players.drop_out_rule: Controllers that are not connected when the game starts drop out. With nobody left, keyboard & mouse plays as player 1.

mouse_pointer.name: Mouse pointer
mouse_pointer.about: The mouse also points for player 1: left click is A, right click is B. The controller keeps working. Only when player 1 plays alone.

access.name: Wii Remote access
access.udev: A Wii Remote is connected, but this user can't open it. Install the udev rule (copy the commands, run them in a terminal), then turn the remote off and on.
access.copied: Udev rule commands copied to the clipboard.
access.in_use: A Wii Remote is connected, but it could not be opened. Close other programs that use it (Dolphin, Steam), then turn the remote off and on.

scanning.name: Continuous scanning
scanning.on: Press 1+2 on a Wii Remote to connect it, here and when a player's Remote drops out of a game.
scanning.off: Off: after 1+2 press Refresh, or pair the Remote with Sync.
scanning.tooltip:
Searching can briefly disturb other Bluetooth devices, such as headphones.
In a game it searches only while a player's Wii Remote is missing.

pairing.name: Bluetooth pairing
pairing.about: Sync pairs a Remote for good: press Sync, then the red SYNC button under its battery cover. It then connects with any button.
pairing.syncing: Syncing: press the red SYNC button under the Remote's battery cover now.

bluetooth.refresh_tooltip: Search once (4 s): press 1+2 on the Remote first.
bluetooth.sync_tooltip:
Pair Wii Remotes for good (about 12 s), as on a Wii.
A paired Remote connects with any button, also in a game.
bluetooth.reset_tooltip:
Forget every Wii Remote Windows remembers, for one that no longer connects
(for example after it was synced with a Wii again). Sync it again afterwards.

wii_remote.title: Wii Remote
wii_remote.about: As in the Wii's own settings. Changes apply when the game starts.

sensor_bar.name: Sensor bar
sensor_bar.about: Where your sensor bar or DolphinBar sits. The game aims the Wii Remote pointer from it.

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
sensitivity.about: How readily the Remote's camera sees the sensor bar (3 is the Wii's default). Raise it when the pointer drops out far from the bar, lower it when lamps or windows disturb it.

speaker.name: Speaker volume
speaker.about: Sounds the game plays on each player's Wii Remote; they play on the TV as well. Off sends no sound to the Remotes.
speaker.tooltip: Speaker sound depends on the Bluetooth link: if it crackles, turn it down or off.

rumble.name: Rumble
rumble.about: The game's rumble on Wii Remotes and gamepads, like the Wii's rumble setting.

strength.name: Gamepad strength
strength.about: How strongly gamepads rumble. A Wii Remote's motor is either on or off.

hotkeys.title: Hotkeys
hotkeys.about: Keys of the game window, whoever plays. Click a hotkey, then press the new key, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. Escape cancels; Backspace or Delete leaves it unused.
hotkeys.tooltip: Click, then press the new keys

show_hud.name: Show the HUD when a match starts
show_hud.about: The scoreboard, player markers and captions. Off starts matches without them, for clean recordings; {{key}} shows them. The Mega Strike meter and its defence always stay.
show_hud.about_no_key: The scoreboard, player markers and captions. Off starts matches without them, for clean recordings; its hotkey shows them. The Mega Strike meter and its defence always stay.

hotkeys.system_keys: Combinations with the Windows or Command key stay with the system.
hotkeys.key_taken: {{key}} presses {{action}} for keyboard & mouse. Give that action another key first, or hold Ctrl, Shift or Alt with it.

test.title: Controller test
test.about: Check a gamepad's buttons and sticks. Assign gamepads to players above.

keyboard.title: Keyboard & mouse
keyboard.about: Click a key, then press the new key or a mouse button (click the key again for the left button). Each action takes up to two. Left and right click are A and B while no action takes them. Changes are saved when you go back.
keyboard.change_tooltip: Click, then press the new key or mouse button
keyboard.add_tooltip: Add a second key or mouse button
keyboard.waiting_tooltip: Press a key or mouse button; click here for the left button

remote.title: Wii Remote
remote.about: Buttons of the keyboard's Wii Remote.

nunchuk.title: Nunchuk & motion
nunchuk.about: The Nunchuk stick and buttons, and the shakes.

mouse.title: Mouse
mouse.about: The screenshot, HUD and fullscreen keys are under Hotkeys on the Controls page.

keyboard.is_hotkey: {{key}} is the hotkey {{hotkey}} (Hotkeys on the Controls page) and cannot be assigned.
keyboard.only_key: {{key}} is the only key of {{action}}. Give that action another key first.

gamepad.title: Gamepad profiles
gamepad.about: Mario Strikers Charged is played with a Wii Remote and Nunchuk. Your controller stands in for them: a profile says which of its buttons presses each Wii button. Pick a profile per gamepad, here or on the Players list. To change a button, select it below and press the new one on the controller. Changes are saved when you go back.

profile.title: Profile
profile.about: Gamepad {{number}} plays with the profile shown here when you go back. Gamepads can share a profile; keep one per player.
profile.invalid_name: A profile name has 1 to 32 characters, without quotes, brackets, = or |, and is not the name of a built-in profile.
profile.not_connected: Gamepad {{number}} is not connected: all profiles are listed, buttons named for {{kind}} controllers.
profile.builtin_copy: Built-in: changing a button below makes your own copy.
profile.unused: No gamepad plays with this profile.
profile.new_made: {{name}} starts as a copy of the profile you were editing.
profile.new_tooltip: A new profile, copied from this one
profile.deleted: Deleted {{name}}. Its gamepads now play with {{default}}.
profile.builtin_delete_tooltip: The built-in profile cannot be deleted
profile.confirm_delete_tooltip: Click again to delete; gamepads using it switch to {{default}}

gamepad.made_for: {{name}} is made for {{kind}} controllers; this gamepad is another kind.
gamepad.now_presses_shared: {{button}} now presses {{action}} and still presses {{others}}: one press does both.
gamepad.builtin_full: {{name}} cannot change and all 16 profiles are in use. Delete one to make your own.
gamepad.copy_made: {{name}} cannot change, so your changes go into {{copy}}, a copy.
gamepad.copy_unassigned: It is not assigned to a gamepad yet.
gamepad.change_tooltip: Select, then press the new button or push a stick on the controller
gamepad.none_tooltip: No button presses this. Select, then press one.
gamepad.both_tooltip: One press does both. Fine where the game never needs them apart.

remote.title: Wii Remote Buttons
remote.about: Press each Wii Remote input, followed by the controller button you want to map to it.

nunchuk.title: Nunchuk & Motion
nunchuk.about: The Nunchuk stick and pointer on the controller's sticks or gyro, the Nunchuk buttons and the shakes.
nunchuk.pointer_note: Point at menu items and Mega Strike shots

sticks.name: Sticks
sticks.about: Which stick moves the Nunchuk stick and which the pointer. Shared: the left stick does both, as the Classic Controller mod on the Wii, and the right stick is free for the D-pad.

gyro_pointer.name: Gyro pointer
gyro_pointer.about: Point by turning the controller, like a Wii Remote, instead of with the stick. For controllers with a gyro, such as PlayStation and Switch Pro controllers.

gyro_speed.name: Gyro speed
gyro_speed.about: At 100%, turning the controller about 25 degrees moves the pointer across the picture.

stick_dpad.about: Push it to press the D-pad: in a match, a deke with the ball and a slide tackle without it.

stick_bound.left_nunchuk: The left stick moves the Nunchuk stick and presses buttons too: pushing it does both.
stick_bound.right_nunchuk: The right stick moves the Nunchuk stick and presses buttons too: pushing it does both.
stick_bound.left_pointer: The left stick moves the pointer and presses buttons too: pushing it does both. With the gyro pointer on, it only presses the buttons.
stick_bound.right_pointer: The right stick moves the pointer and presses buttons too: pushing it does both. With the gyro pointer on, it only presses the buttons.

gyro_preview.connect: Connect gamepad {{number}} to try the gyro here.
gyro_preview.no_gyro_left: {{name}} has no gyro: its left stick moves the pointer instead.
gyro_preview.no_gyro_right: {{name}} has no gyro: its right stick moves the pointer instead.

dead_zones.title: Dead zones & triggers
dead_zones.about: How far a stick or trigger must move before it counts. Try it on the controller below.

octagon.name: Real Nunchuk stick
octagon.about: The Nunchuk stick plays like a real one: its octagonal edge and the game's own dead zone, which snaps nearly straight pushes straight. The dead zones below then shape the pointer stick only.

inner.name: Inner dead zone
inner.about: The stick rests until it is tilted this far. Raise it if a worn stick drifts.

outer.name: Outer dead zone
outer.about: From this tilt on the stick is pushed all the way. 71% plays like a Nunchuk on the Wii; higher leaves more room for fine moves and slow pointing.

trigger.name: Trigger press point
trigger.about: A trigger presses its button past this much of its travel.

dead_zones.connect: Connect gamepad {{number}} to try these here.

gamepad.reset_tooltip: Buttons, sticks, gyro, dead zones and triggers as in {{default}}

pad_tooltip.about: Your controller's button for each Wii input. Click to change.
pad_tooltip.feel: Stick dead zones {{inner}}-{{outer}}%, triggers press at {{trigger}}%
pad_tooltip.feel_gyro: Stick dead zones {{inner}}-{{outer}}%, triggers press at {{trigger}}%, gyro speed {{gyro}}%

gameplay.title: Gameplay
gameplay.about: Optional tweaks that change the original game. With all of them off, the game plays as on the Wii.
gameplay.all_tweaks_tooltip: Turn all gameplay tweaks on or off.

side.name: Side
side.about: The team whose captain and sidekicks are robots.

disc.name: GameCube disc
disc.none_found: None found in your game folder. Choose your Super Mario Strikers image.

super_team.uses_found: The Super Team uses {{file}} from your game folder.
super_team.not_strikers: {{file}} is not a Super Mario Strikers (GameCube) image.

item.name: Item
item.about: The item your team starts every kickoff with. It stays after you use it. A single shell, banana or Bob-omb comes out medium or giant at random, a giant one always giant.

captain.name: Captain
captain.about: Start training's captain, with their sidekicks from the Teams page.

side.name: Your team
side.about: The side you play: home or away. Controller 1 plays it.

opponent_captain.name: Opponent captain
opponent_captain.about: The other team's captain, with their sidekicks from the Teams page. The same as yours plays as Bowser, or Mario against Bowser.

opponent_fielders.name: Opponent fielders
opponent_fielders.about: How many of the other team's four fielders play, the captain last to go; the rest vanish at every kickoff, as in the Strikers 101 lessons.

opponent_skill.name: Opponent skill
opponent_skill.about: How well the other team's players play. Training is the level of the Strikers 101 lessons, below Rookie.

opponent_goalie.name: Opponent goalie
opponent_goalie.about: Whether the other team's goalie plays. Off, the goal is empty.

skip_goals.name: Skip intro and replays
skip_goals.about: The match starts at the kickoff, and a goal goes straight to the next one, without its celebration and replay. A Mega Strike's goal keeps its own.

start.name: Start training
start.about: Starts the game straight into a match to 10 goals that never ends on them, past the intro and the menus.

mods.title: Mods
mods.about: Texture packs replace the game's textures with sharper ones. They change only how the game looks.

texture_packs.name: Texture packs
texture_packs.about: Texture packs made for Dolphin, from the folder below. Drop a pack's folder or .zip file onto this page to add it.

folder.missing: Not there yet: Open makes it, and a dropped pack goes into it
folder.click_tooltip: Click to select another texture packs folder.
folder.open_tooltip: Show the folder (it is made when missing).

drop.title: Drop a texture pack here
drop.about: A pack's folder (such as R4Q) or its .zip file: it is copied into the folder above.

mods.order_note: Drag a pack to change the order: where two packs replace the same texture, the higher one wins.

dump.name: Dump textures
dump.about: For pack makers: each texture no pack replaces is saved to data/texture_dumps, named as texture packs need it. Takes disk space and can make the game stutter.
dump.not_made: Made when the game first dumps a texture.

mods.bug_report_note: Tweaks and texture packs apply when the game starts. For a bug report, try again with the tweaks off (or start the game with --no-tweaks) and without texture packs to check whether one of them is involved.
mods.pack_added: {{pack}} was added to your texture packs.
mods.already_in_folder: {{pack}} is already in your texture packs folder.
mods.folder_has_pack: Your texture packs folder already has a {{pack}}.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.about: Troubleshooting and development options. The defaults suit most players.

launcher_size.name: Launcher size
launcher_size.about: Scales this launcher. Automatic follows your display's scaling setting.

reopen.name: Reopen after the game
reopen.about: Opens the launcher again when you close the game.

updates.title: Updates
updates.about: Each start of the launcher installs a newer build by itself. A release plays online only while it is the newest one.

api.name: Graphics API
api.about: Used the next time you start the game.
api.about_windows: Automatic uses Vulkan, or DirectX 12 when Vulkan cannot start. Used the next time you start the game.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics & analytics
diagnostics.about: Local tools for investigating performance and graphics issues.

performance_stats.name: Performance stats
performance_stats.about: Records frame times for each game session, with the arena and settings, and a summary per arena. Saves a CSV and summary in the logs folder; testers can share them.

shader_cache.name: Shader cache
shader_cache.about: Clears compiled shaders for all graphics APIs. The next launch prepares them again.
shader_cache.cleared: Shader cache cleared. Graphics will be prepared again on the next launch.
shader_cache.empty: The shader cache is already empty.

validation.name: API validation
validation.about: Checks every graphics call for errors. Useful for bug reports, but slower.

log_detail.name: Log detail
log_detail.about: Which messages reach the console: errors, warnings, info or debug.

verbose.name: Verbose console
verbose.about: Also prints development traces and the game's own debug output. Useful for bug reports.

log_window.name: Log window
log_window.about: Shows the log in a separate window while Recharged runs, for testing. Closing it doesn't stop the game.

command.name: Launch command
command.about: Copies a command line that starts the game with these settings.
command.copied: Launch command copied to the clipboard.

defaults.name: Restore defaults
defaults.about: Resets every setting except your game image and game folder. Save to keep the result.
defaults.restored: Defaults restored. Save to keep them.

thanks.title: Thank you
thanks.about: Recharged is shaped by the people who play it.

special.about: For intense testing, build after build.

reporters.about: Everyone who reported a problem or asked for a feature on GitHub. Every issue makes Recharged better: this is how we roll!

decompilation.about: To the contributors of the decompilation, who helped bring it over the last miles.

community.title: Mario Strikers on Discord
community.about: The central hub of Mario Strikers players: tournaments, matchmaking and league play across the series, with fans, competitors and creators from around the world.
community.thanks: Thank you for the matches, the feedback and all the enthusiasm!

foundations.title: Built on
foundations.decompilation_about: Recharged compiles the reconstructed C/C++ source of Mario Strikers Charged to native code. The original game logic runs unchanged; Recharged provides the platform underneath it: graphics, audio, input, files and timing.
foundations.aurora_about: Aurora by Luke Street provides the GameCube/Wii platform layer the game runs on: GX graphics on modern GPUs, plus windowing, input and system services.
foundations.unofficial: Unofficial project, not affiliated with Nintendo or Next Level Games. You need your own copy of the game.

build.title: This build
build.about: For a bug report: copy these details and attach the log.
build.copied: Build details copied to the clipboard.
